metadata.subject: DBMS
metadata.title: Connect Related Tables
metadata.description: Choose related columns and predict every row produced by an INNER or LEFT JOIN.

learning_objectives: Explain why rows match on related key values.
Predict one-to-many and unmatched JOIN output.
Distinguish INNER JOIN from LEFT JOIN.

mission.title: Build a JOIN from source rows
mission.description: Choose the relationship, predict every matching pair, then run the evaluator.

introduction.title: A JOIN follows shared values
introduction.content: Related tables store different facts. A JOIN compares chosen columns and combines rows only when their key values satisfy the join rule.
points: Equal key values can create a row pair.
One row may match several rows.
INNER and LEFT JOIN handle unmatched rows differently.

worked_example.title: Follow the keys, not the row positions
worked_example.content: Suppose student 101 is Ana and two enrollment records also contain 101.

steps.explanation: Equal keys make one valid pair.
The same left row can make another valid pair.
An INNER JOIN omits source rows that never find a match.

worked_example.conclusion: JOIN output comes from every matching combination; duplicate keys must not be deduplicated.

next.title: Now you try.
next.content: Choose the relationship and predict the exact source-row pairs.

action_explanations.choose-left-column: The left join column supplies one side of each comparison.
action_explanations.choose-right-column: The right join column supplies the related values.
action_explanations.choose-join-type: The join type decides what happens to unmatched rows.
action_explanations.predict-matches: Each selected pair predicts one possible output row.
action_explanations.run-join: The evaluator compared actual values and constructed every valid output row.

goal.instruction: Build an INNER JOIN that relates students to enrollments by student_id.
Build a LEFT JOIN that keeps every author and matches books by author_id.

actions.label: Build, predict, and run the JOIN

challenge.title: LEFT JOIN challenge
challenge.start_message: Keep every left row while predicting actual matches.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep exploring the relationship.

phases.title: Construct the LEFT JOIN
phases.instruction: Choose related columns and predict all result-row pairs, including unmatched left rows.
phases.feedback: Compare every left key with every right key; do not deduplicate repeated matches.

items.content: Compare the values, not row positions.

phases.title: Practice INNER JOIN
phases.instruction: Choose the related columns and predict every match.
phases.feedback: Select exactly the equal-key row pairs.

phases.title: Apply one-to-many matching
phases.feedback: One left row may contribute several output rows.

guidance.start_message: Solve a LEFT JOIN with unmatched source rows.

phases.title: Solve LEFT JOIN
phases.instruction: Predict matches and NULL-side rows without hints.
phases.feedback: Every left row remains; unmatched right values become NULL.

guidance.start_message: Choose between INNER and LEFT semantics independently.

phases.title: Master JOIN reasoning
phases.instruction: Interpret the generated rule and predict every result row.
phases.feedback: Recheck the join type, columns, and every row combination.

thinking.title: Predict a hidden JOIN result
thinking.instruction: Choose the relationship and list every source-row pair before any result table is revealed.
thinking.do_not_execute: Compare all keys mentally. Duplicate values can create multiple output rows.

prediction_fields.label: Join type
prediction_fields.prompt: Which join type does the goal require?

prediction_fields.label: Left column
prediction_fields.prompt: Enter the left join column name.

prediction_fields.label: Right column
prediction_fields.prompt: Enter the right join column name.

prediction_fields.label: Result row pairs
prediction_fields.prompt: List pair IDs separated by commas, or NONE.

feedback.incorrect: Review each field and equal-key combination.

quiz.question: Why can one left row produce multiple INNER JOIN rows?
options: Several right rows can have the same matching key

discovery.title: JOIN discovery
discovery.summary: A JOIN computes row combinations from actual equality between the chosen key columns.

sections.title: Matching
sections.content: Rows combine because their selected key values satisfy the join condition.

sections.title: One-to-many
sections.content: One row can match several rows and therefore create several output rows.

sections.title: INNER vs LEFT
sections.content: INNER omits unmatched rows; LEFT preserves unmatched left rows with NULL right values.

alternate_explanations.title: Match claim tickets
alternate_explanations.content: A JOIN is like matching every bag to every claim ticket with the same number.

alternate_explanations.title: Follow 101
alternate_explanations.content: If student 101 has two enrollment rows, INNER JOIN produces two combined rows for that student.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why can duplicate join keys create several result rows?
recall.model_answer: The evaluator creates one result row for every valid left-right matching combination.
